abstract:
Brain somatic mutations are a major cause of epileptogenic focal cortical malformations. Hyaline astrocytic inclusions represent a rare neuropathological finding in epilepsy.
We analyzed eight patients undergoing surgery for drug-resistant focal epilepsy associated with astrocytic inclusions, combining bulk and single-nucleus genomic analyses, cell-type-specific genetic profiling, neuropathological characterization, and electrophysiological recordings to establish genotype-neuropathology correlations.
Microelectrode array recordings from cortical slices from one patient revealed spontaneous abnormal network activity in regions without astrocytic inclusions. Multilayered genomic analysis of surgical brain tissue, including single-nucleus sequencing, identified mosaic chromosome 1q copy-number gains in all eight cases, with chr1q tetrasomies confirmed in six. In four cases, the supernumerary chromosome 1q was of maternal origin, and long-read haplotyping in a patient-parent trio supported a novel mechanism of meiosis II chromosome missegregation. Chr1q gains were enriched in inclusion-bearing astrocytes, linking chromosomal aneuploidy to neuropathology. Finally, we developed a targeted sequencing panel enabling the detection of chr1q gains in surgical brain samples, including samples obtained from presurgical stereo-EEG electrodes.
Together, these findings support postzygotic rescue of a maternal meiotic error in non-neural lineages as a mechanism of pathogenic brain mosaicism and define mosaic chr1q gain as a distinct cause of epilepsy.
